title: No mail delivery June 19 in Indiana for Juneteenth holiday - AOL
snippet: There will be no retail service or mail delivery in Indiana on June 19, but kiosks and online services will allow some shipping and tracking tasks.
extractedText: No mail delivery June 19 in Indiana for Juneteenth holidayJane Imbody, Richmond Paladium-ItemFri, June 12, 2026 at 1:54 PM UTC0No mail delivery June 19 in Indiana for Juneteenth holidayPost offices in Indiana will close in observance of Juneteenth on June 19, pausing regular mail delivery and retail services.The U.S. Postal Service said operations will resume June 20, when customers can again access in-person services at retail locations, according to a community announcement.Customers will still be able to access several services online and through self-service kiosks when physical locations are closed.What services remain availablePostal officials said many products and services remain accessible through usps.com and automated kiosks located in select lobbies nationwide.Those kiosks allow customers to print postage for Priority Mail, Priority Mail Express and international shipments, purchase stamps, weigh and mail packages, and retrieve package tracking details.Expanded self-service optionsAs part of ongoing modernization efforts, USPS locations are adding additional self-service features, according to the announcement.AdvertisementThese may include rapid dropoff stations for customers who already created and printed shipping labels online, as well as machines that allow label printing using merchant-provided QR codes.Some locations also offer USPS Smart Lockers, which provide options for both package pickup and dropoff.Many kiosks operate around the clock, offering access to postal services even when traditional counters are closed.For more information about available services, customers can visit usps.com.This story was created with the assistance of Artificial Intelligence (AI). Journalists were involved in every step of the information gathering, review, editing and publishing process. Learn more at cm.usatoday.com/ethical-conduct.This article originally appeared on Richmond Palladium-Item: USPS Juneteenth schedule in Indiana: What to know
